chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Ibn Bukayr from al-Hasan al-Attar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who commanded his slave to perform Umrah up to Hajj (Tamattu'), is it upon him to slaughter an animal on his behalf? He said: 'No, indeed Allah the Exalted says: A slave who has no power over anything.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in it is that slaughtering is not obligatory upon him, and he is free to choose between it and commanding him to fast. What was narrated indicates this:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the master's obligation to slaughter or fast when his slave performs Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a master is not strictly obligated to slaughter a sacrificial animal for a slave who performs Tamattu' Hajj, citing the Quranic principle that a slave lacks independent capacity ('power'). Shaykh al-Tusi notes the master retains discretion to choose between slaughter or commanding the slave to fast, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the flexibility of expiation (Kaffarah) based on the dependent's financial status.
